q: Does the GLOBLE giant-loop clustering assumption hold when DSB spatial distributions are taken from measured Hi-C / chromatin-loop maps rather than the model's idealized uniform ~2 Mbp domains?
basis: The replication reproduces every equation-level claim but never tests the core biophysical premise (that lethality arises from DSB clustering within higher-order chromatin loops). The model assumes uniform giant loops; real loop-domain sizes vary by 1-2 orders of magnitude across cell types and cell-cycle phase.
next_steps: Drive the GLOBLE clustering kernel with cell-line-specific loop-domain size distributions from published Hi-C data (e.g. GM12878, HeLa, mES) and test whether the fitted epsilon_i/epsilon_c ratios track measured loop statistics rather than being free fit parameters. A positive result would upgrade GLOBLE from a fitting model to a mechanistic predictor.

q: Is the exact pointwise overlay against measured cell-survival curves (blocked Claim 7) recoverable by re-digitizing the paper's own figure PDFs, and if so does GLOBLE still fit within experimental error across all 17 lines?
basis: Claim 7 is the only empirical test and it is BLOCKED because the authors' digitized experimental points (produced with GetData Graph Digitalizer) were never distributed. Every other claim is a self-consistency or closed-form check, so the model's agreement with actual biology remains unverified in this reproduction.
next_steps: Run a controlled digitization pass (WebPlotDigitizer) on the high-resolution figure files for all plotted survival curves, propagate digitization uncertainty, and compute chi-square goodness-of-fit of GLOBLE (with Table-2 params, no refitting) against the recovered points. Cross-check against the primary source papers (Steel 1987, Stephens 1987, Holmes 1990, Ruiz de Almodovar 1994).

q: Why does the paper's median HLT_i (0.458 h) match only the split-dose column and not the dose-rate column (0.487 h), and does this column-dependence signal a real difference in repair kinetics probed by the two assay types?
basis: Claim A reproduced 0.458 h exactly for the split-dose column but the dose-rate column median is 0.487 h; the paper text quotes 0.458 h without specifying a column. This ambiguity was surfaced only because the replication computed both.
next_steps: Determine whether the two columns are fit to genuinely different experimental datasets (split-dose recovery vs continuous low-dose-rate) and test whether a single HLT_i can jointly fit both assay types per cell line, or whether the ~6% systematic difference reflects a real dual-timescale repair process the single-half-life model cannot capture.

q: At what dose rate does the high-dose-rate 'instantaneous' limit break down for clinically relevant fractionation, and does GLOBLE's dose-rate dependence remain accurate in the FLASH regime (>40 Gy/s)?
basis: Claim E showed the static-GLOBLE limit only converges within tolerance at >=10^6 Gy/h; at 10^4 Gy/h it fails for short-HLT_i lines like CHO K1. Conventional and FLASH radiotherapy sit far below 10^6 Gy/h.
next_steps: Map the convergence residual as a continuous function of dose rate for each cell line's HLT_i, identify the crossover dose rate where clustering kinetics matter, and test GLOBLE predictions against emerging FLASH cell-survival datasets where dose-rate effects are hypothesized to invert.

q: Can the GLOBLE five-level DSB-clustering framework be extended from photons to mixed-LET / ion beams without abandoning the giant-loop assumption, and does the epsilon_i << epsilon_c ordering survive at high LET?
basis: The replication confirmed epsilon_i << epsilon_c for 22/22 photon parameter sets (Claim A), but photons produce sparse, roughly random DSB distributions. High-LET tracks produce dense, correlated DSB clusters that may violate the model's separation of isolated vs clustered lesion channels.
next_steps: Couple GLOBLE's loop-clustering formalism to a track-structure DSB generator (e.g. from the sibling ion-beam LUCID replications), recompute epsilon_i/epsilon_c as a function of LET, and test whether the isolated-lesion channel becomes negligible (a testable prediction) or whether a new intra-track clustering term is required.
